title: Freeze choices before one final test report
description: A quick reference for validation-selected state, the test-only gate, fair token weighting, evaluation provenance, immutable reporting, and like-for-like comparison.

terms.definition: The planned model checkpoint chosen using validation evidence before any test result is available.
The complete selected decoder snapshot after every model and data choice is sealed; test scores may describe it but cannot change it.

The once-only post-selection protocol that verifies held-out test role and provenance before scoring, consumes test access when scoring begins, and prevents test evidence from becoming a selection signal.
The reporting-only pass over held-out test data after selection closes; its result cannot choose a checkpoint or tune another decision.
Total negative log likelihood divided by the number of aligned target tokens, so longer documents contribute in proportion to their targets.
The exponential of mean negative log likelihood, expressing average multiplicative uncertainty per target token.
One causal input and observed next-token target at a stable document, window, and position, including repetitions from overlapping windows.
The shared corpus, split, tokenizer, and context identity binding the selected decoder, baseline, and test epoch.
Scoring with graph construction disabled and with decoder parameters and gradient bits verified unchanged afterward.
A versioned record of final test provenance, aligned targets, scores, one-use evidence, and state-preservation checks, fixed after selection closes.
An add-one bigram fitted only on the same training token slices and sealed before test access.
A comparison where both models score the same ordered target slots, including every repetition from overlapping decoder windows.
